newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Klima sees CA decision after Christmas.
newsitem.headline: Klima sees CA decision after Christmas.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima said on Thursday a final decision on the sale of Creditanstalt-Bankverein would be made between Christmas and New Year.

"The decision will probably be made between Christmas and New Year," Social Democrat Klima said, contradicting conservative Economy Minister Johann Farnleitner who earlier on Thursday told reporters a decision could be expected before the weekend.

"We don't let ourselves be pressured," a spokesman for Klima told Reuters. He added JP Morgan, the government's advisor in the sale, had yet to provide evaluations of the offers for the state's 70 percent voting stake in the bank.
Bank Austria has topped the bidding for Creditanstalt, reportedly putting up more than 15 billion schillings. At current market prices the state's holding is worth 14.5 billion.
It is up against rival bids from a consortium led by Italian controlled insurer EA-Generali and 79-year-old former supermarket tycoon Karl Wlaschek.
Farnleitner, a member of the conservative People's Party, has opposed "socialist" Bank Austria's takeover plans. Klima has insisted the government's Creditanstalt stake must go to the best bidder.
